title: Variational formulation of a general dissipative fluid system with differential forms
summary: This work is devoted to the study of dissipative fluid systems, through the lens of a geometric variational formulation. Building upon previous works extending Hamilton's principle to non-equilibrium thermodynamics, the present method incorporates an arbitrary number of additional variables expressed as differential forms. Dissipation sources, thermodynamic flux closures, and their associated boundary conditions are also all expressed in this differential-form framework. The resulting equations are consistent with the fundamental laws of thermodynamics, namely conservation of total energy…
